Ares (Ancient) is the Greek god of war and courage.

This Indian National Congress politician became the 18th Chief Minister of the state of Karnataka in June 2026, after previously serving as its Deputy Chief Minister — who is he?

Domingo Faustino Sarmiento (15 February 1811 - 11 September 1888) was President of Argentina from 1868 to 1874.

Nicknamed Bubi, this German pilot flew 1,404 combat missions and was credited with 352 kills, making him the most successful fighter ace in the history of aerial warfare — yet he was never shot down by direct enemy fire. Who was he?
Erich Hartmann (19 April 1922 - 20 September 1993), nicknamed Bubi, was a German fighter pilot during World War II and the most successful fighter ace in the history of aerial warfare.
This New Hampshire-born Democrat — son of a state governor — inflamed the slavery crisis by signing the Kansas-Nebraska Act during his single term in the 1850s. Who was he?
Franklin Pierce (November 23, 1804 - October 8, 1869) was the 14th president of the United States, serving from 1853 to 1857.

Giorgio Napolitano (29 June 1925 - 22 September 2023) was an Italian politician who served as the president of Italy from 2006 to 2015.
This ancient Babylonian king conquered the rival city-states of Larsa, Eshnunna, and Mari during his reign in the 18th century BC, succeeding his father who abdicated due to poor health — who is he?
Hammurabi (c. 1810 BC - c. 1750 BC), also spelled Hammurapi, was the sixth Amorite king of Babylon, reigning from c. 1792 to c. 1750 BC.

A Finnish president and tireless diplomat — UN Commissioner for Namibia, special envoy for Kosovo — he won the 2008 Nobel Peace Prize for his peace work; who was he?
Martti Ahtisaari (23 June 1937 - 16 October 2023) was a Finnish politician and diplomat who was the president of Finland from 1994 to 2000.
He became General Secretary of the Communist Party in 1985 and drifted toward social democracy by the early 1990s — all while presiding over the Soviet Union's last years. Who was he?
Mikhail Gorbachev (2 March 1931 - 30 August 2022) was a Soviet and Russian politician who was the last leader of the Soviet Union from 1985 until the country's dissolution in 1991.

Formed from the union of two smaller kingdoms after a seventh-century murder, this early medieval realm spanned modern Northern England and Southern Scotland until 1066 — what was it?
Northumbria was an early medieval English kingdom, existing between 654 and 1066 AD, spanning modern-day Northern England and Southern Scotland.

Jeremiah: Biblical prophet. Jeremiah (c. 650 – c. 570 BC), also called Jeremias, and occasionally in older English texts Jeremy, was one of the major prophets of the Hebrew Bible.

Walter Raleigh: English statesman and explorer (1552–1618)
Starting in his father's grocery business, this English industrialist built an empire on Sunlight Soap and brands like Lux and Lifebuoy through the firm he founded with his brother — who was he?
William Lever, 1st Viscount Leverhulme: English industrialist, philanthropist and politician (1851–1925)

Sparked by rising fuel prices and an online petition with nearly a million signatures, these weekly French demonstrations began in November 2018, their protesters named for the high-visibility garment they wore. What movement was it?
Yellow vests protests: 2018 social movement started in France.
Nicknamed 'The Acquitator' for his string of courtroom wins as a criminal defense lawyer, he served as France's Minister of Justice from 2020 to 2024 — who is he?
Éric Dupond-Moretti: French-Italian politician and lawyer (born 1961)
Which one below was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four. Benjamin Banneker (November 9, 1731 – October 19, 1806) was an American naturalist, mathematician, astronomer and almanac author.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
Earth (formed ~4.54 billion years ago) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these is a physicist?
John Logie Baird is a physicist. In 1928, the Baird Television Development Company achieved the first transatlantic television transmission.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
What is the atomic number of Nihonium?
Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.
What is the atomic number of Strontium?
Strontium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sr and atomic number 38.
In what year did Edward Teller die?
Edward Teller: Born in Austria-Hungary in 1908, Teller emigrated to the US in the 1930s, one of the many so-called "Martians", a group of Hungarian scientist émigrés.
In what year was Oxygen discovered?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
Potassium chloride: Pfizer. Potassium chloride (KCl, or potassium salt) is a metal halide salt composed of potassium and chlorine.
Rendang: Indonesia. It refers to both a cooking method of frying and the dish cooked in that way.
Who is credited with discovering Musca?
Musca: Petrus Plancius. Musca (Latin for 'the fly') is a small constellation in the deep southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Testosterone?
Testosterone: János Freud. Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone and androgen in males.
Who is credited with discovering Cyanoacrylate?
Cyanoacrylate: Harry Coover. The cyanoacrylate group in the monomer rapidly polymerizes in the presence of water to form long, strong chains.
Who is credited with discovering Rubidium?
Rubidium: Robert Bunsen. Rubidium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rb and atomic number 37.
In chemistry, this class is defined by an −OH group that lends water-loving properties to otherwise water-shy hydrocarbons, spanning everything from ethanol to sugar versions — what is it?
Alcohol (chemistry) (from Arabic al-kul 'the kohl') is a type of organic compound that carries at least one hydroxyl (OH) functional group bound to a saturated carbon atom.
A balloon-like bulge at a weakened patch of vessel wall, it can turn lethal in the brain's circle of Willis or the aorta if it bursts — what is this?
Aneurysm is an outward bulging, likened to a bubble or balloon, caused by a localized, abnormal, weak spot on a blood vessel wall.
With almost 500 species in the daisy family, this large plant genus includes mugwort, wormwood, and sagebrush, and is sometimes confused with a related genus of sages — which genus?
Artemisia (plant) (art--) is a large, diverse genus of plants belonging to the daisy family, Asteraceae, with almost 500 species.

This genus of deciduous trees includes 14 species across two subgenera, one found only in East Asia with low, multi-trunked growth, the other spanning Europe, Asia, and eastern North America. What tree genus is this?

Beech (genus Fagus) is a genus of deciduous trees in the family Fagaceae, native to subtropical (accessory forest element) and temperate (as dominant element of mesophytic forests) Eurasia and North America.
Native to North America and introduced to Europe in the 1930s, these prostrate shrubs in the genus Vaccinium range from 4 inches to 13 feet tall — what fruit is it?
Blueberry are a widely distributed and widespread group of perennial flowering plants with blue or purple berries.
This flammable, colorless alkane gas with the formula C4H10 takes its name from a Greek word for butter, via butyric acid — what is it?
Butane is an alkane with the formula C4H10. Butane exists as two isomers, n-butane, CH3CH2CH2CH3 and iso-butane, (CH3)3CH.
This large, stocky black corvid fills a niche across Eurasia comparable to a similar bird found in North America, but is bigger and huskier than its transatlantic counterpart — what species is it?
Carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.
Defined by a hollow dorsal nerve cord, an endostyle, and a post-anal tail at some point in life, this phylum spans vertebrates, tunicates, and lancelets alike — which option fits?
Chordate is a bilaterian animal belonging to the phylum Chordata (kor-).
This towering annual in the daisy family yields seeds in two flavors — oilseed (the world's fourth most-used vegetable oil) and the confectionary kind you crack as a snack — which plant?
Common sunflower (Helianthus annuus) is a large annual forb in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Grown from tubers and known by the folk name 'sowbread,' this Primulaceae genus features flowers with distinctively upswept petals — which plant genus?
Cyclamen is a genus of 25 species of perennial flowering plants in the family Primulaceae.
This Russian chemist's great law let him predict three undiscovered elements — germanium, gallium, and scandium — and a synthetic element now bears his name; who was he?
Which American toy magnate teamed up with his wife Ruth to co-found Mattel and dream up Hot Wheels and Barbie?
Elliot Handler (April 9, 1916 - July 21, 2011) was an American inventor, business magnate, and the co-founder of Mattel.
Botanists use this word for any plant whose leaves stay green and functional through every season, never going bare like a deciduous tree — what is it?
Evergreen is a plant which has foliage that remains green and functional throughout the year.
This American physician-scientist discovered genes tied to several diseases, led the Human Genome Project, and went on to direct the NIH under three presidents — who is he?
Francis Collins (born April 14, 1950) is an American physician-scientist who discovered the genes associated with a number of diseases and led the Human Genome Project.

Built from epithelial tissue with a supporting connective-tissue capsule, this kind of structure secretes hormones straight into the blood if it's ductless, or through a duct to a cavity or surface if not — what is it called?
Gland is a cell or an organ in an animal's body that produces and secretes different substances that the organism needs, either into the bloodstream or into a body cavity or outer surface.
Named for a flattened, laterally extended head shape called a cephalofoil, with eyes placed at each end of the T, this family of sharks includes species mostly grouped in one genus — which sharks?

Hammerhead shark are a group of sharks that form the family Sphyrnidae, named for the unusual and distinctive form of their heads, which are flattened and laterally extended into a cephalofoil (a T-shape or "hammer").
This perennial root vegetable, a relative of mustard, wasabi, broccoli, and cabbage, is grated and used worldwide as a pungent spice and condiment — what plant is it?
This contagious bacterial skin infection most often shows up as yellowish crusts on a child's face, arms, or legs, and spreads easily in crowded day cares and contact sports — what is it?
Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection that involves the superficial skin.
This American psychiatrist and Communist Party USA member is best remembered today for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer — who was she?
Jean Tatlock (February 21, 1914 - January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
Native to eastern and southern Africa, this flowering shrub is the sole species in its genus and has a documented history of cultivation dating back to Ethiopia's Harar region. Name the plant?
Khat (Catha edulis), also known as Bushman's tea, especially in South Africa, is a species of flowering plant in the family Celastraceae, and the sole species in genus Catha.
This leafy member of the daisy family is eaten raw in salads and sandwiches, though one Asian variety, celtuce, is grown instead for its edible stem — what is it?
Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) is an annual plant of the family Asteraceae mostly grown as a leaf vegetable.
Often caused by cigarette smoking or inhaled chemicals damaging airway cell DNA, this malignant tumor often shows no symptoms until it has already spread. What disease is it?
Lung cancer is a malignant tumor that originates in the tissues of the lungs.

This prehistoric proboscidean's molars have ridge-like zygodont cusps very different from a mammoth's, and its genus diverged from elephant ancestors over 28 million years ago in the Oligocene — which animal?

Mastodon (from Ancient Greek (masts) 'breast' and (odos) 'tooth') is a member of the genus Mammut (German for 'mammoth'), which was endemic to North America and lived from the late Miocene to the early Holocene.
Carrying NATO's 'Hind' codename and its crews' affectionate 'flying tank,' this Soviet machine is both an attack craft and a low-capacity troop carrier. What is it?
Mil Mi-24 (NATO reporting name: Hind) is a large helicopter gunship, attack helicopter and low-capacity troop transport with room for eight passengers.
When the radial fibres of the iris over-dilate the pupil beyond its normal light response, what do doctors call this condition?
Mydriasis is the dilation of the pupil, usually having a non-physiological cause, or sometimes a physiological pupillary response.

Born in New York to Jewish Holocaust-survivor parents, this Princeton-trained political scientist studies the politics of the Holocaust and the Israeli–Palestinian conflict — and his 2007 DePaul tenure fight made headlines. Who is he?
Norman Finkelstein (born December 8, 1953) is an American political scientist and activist.
Part of the Bovidae family, this genus of seven social species is better known simply as sheep, all thought to trace back to the wild mouflon — which genus?
Ovis is a genus of mammals, part of the Caprinae subfamily of the ruminant family Bovidae.

Which American chemist was the first to synthesize physostigmine and pioneered making progesterone and testosterone from plant sterols — even starting a company to extract steroid intermediates from wild Mexican yams?
Percy Lavon Julian (April 11, 1899 - April 19, 1975) was an American research chemist and a pioneer in the chemical synthesis of medicinal drugs from plants.
This zodiac sign's Latin name means 'fishes,' and it's where the ecliptic crosses the celestial equator near the March equinox — which one?
Pisces (constellation) is a constellation of the zodiac. It is between Aquarius, of similar size, to the southwest and Aries, which is smaller, to the east.

This mammal genus includes a familiar, masked, ring-tailed nocturnal visitor common across North America, plus two lesser-known tropical relatives; its closest kin are the ring-tailed cats and cacomistles. What animal is this?
Procyon (genus) is a genus of nocturnal mammals comprising three species commonly known as raccoons in the family Procyonidae.
A medium-sized tropical tree native to Southeast Asia, it's a close relative of the lychee and longan and shares its name with the edible fruit it bears — what is it?
Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum) is a medium-sized tropical tree in the family Sapindaceae.
Native to West Africa and later naturalized across Asia and the West Indies, this plant's stems yield fibre while its calyces are steeped for a popular infusion — what is it?
Roselle (plant) (Sabdariffa gossypiifolia) is a species of flowering plant in the genus Sabdariffa that is native to Africa, most likely West Africa.
With segmented bony armor, an upright posture, and a curling prehensile tail, these 46 species of tiny bony fish are cousins to the pipefishes and seadragons — what are they?
Seahorse (also written sea-horse and sea horse) is any of 46 species of small marine bony fish in the genus Hippocampus.
Doctors recommend covering your elbow rather than your hands to block this involuntary, explosive rush of air from spreading illness through the air. What is this reflex called?
Sneeze (also known as sternutation) is a semi-autonomous, convulsive expulsion of air from the lungs through the nose and mouth, usually caused by foreign particles irritating the nasal mucosa.
A small Eurasian mustelid that turns brilliant white in winter, this animal's coat — known as ermine — once draped Catholic monarchs and the Infant Jesus of Prague — what is it?
Stoat (Mustela erminea), also known as the Eurasian ermine or ermine, is a species of mustelid native to Eurasia and the northern regions of North America.
This protective cap of repetitive nucleotide sequences guards the ends of eukaryotic chromosomes from progressive degradation — what is it called?
Telomere (from Ancient Greek (tlos) 'end' and (mros) 'part') is a region of repetitive nucleotide sequences associated with specialized proteins at the ends of linear chromosomes (see Sequences).
Dolphins, porpoises, beaked whales and sperm whales all belong to this cetacean group that diverged from baleen whales around 34 million years ago — what's the collective name?

Toothed whale (also called odontocetes, systematic name Odontoceti) are a parvorder of cetaceans that includes dolphins, porpoises, and all other whales with teeth, such as beaked whales and the sperm whales.
This phenolic aldehyde is the primary component of the vanilla bean's extract — and its synthetic version now flavors more foods than the natural one does. What is it?
Vanillin is an organic compound with the molecular formula C8H8O3.
This Austrian physicist earned a 1945 Nobel Prize for the exclusion principle and, in 1930, proposed the existence of what would become known as the neutrino — who is he?
Wolfgang Pauli (25 April 1900 - 15 December 1958) was an Austrian theoretical physicist and a pioneer of quantum mechanics.

Introduced to the British Isles by 1500 and known there simply as 'sycamore,' this wind-tolerant maple from Central Europe can grow to 35 metres and has turned invasive in North America and Australia — which species?
Acer pseudoplatanus: Species of maple tree. It is a large deciduous, broad-leaved tree, tolerant of wind and coastal exposure.
Launched to challenge the Boeing 747, this is the world's largest passenger airliner and the only full-length double-deck jet — which aircraft, unveiled in Toulouse in 2005?
This American economist shared the 2012 Nobel for the theory of stable allocations and "market design" — applying economic theory to real-world matching problems; who is he?

This psychological term describes reduced motivation or ability to experience pleasure, recognized in the DSM-5 as a component of depressive, substance-related, psychotic, and personality disorders. What is it called?
Its name comes from Greek roots meaning 'chief' and 'creator,' and historians often identify whole vanished civilizations by what survives of this visual art. What is it?
Architecture: Art and technique of designing buildings.
A cousin of the tomato and potato, this European nightshade is so toxic — via atropine and scopolamine — that even handling it can harm you; its other common name is "belladonna." What's the plant?
Atropa bella-donna: Deadly nightshade, a flowering plant.
First flown in 1947 with a distinctive V-tail, this single-engine aircraft holds the record for the longest continuous production run in aviation history — which model?
Beechcraft Bonanza: Family of single engine American light aircraft, first flown in 1945.
Recognizable by its angled wings and forked tail, this scavenging bird of prey is thought to be the world's most abundant raptor, with a global population topping six million — which bird?
Black kite: Species of bird. The black kite or fire kite (Milvus migrans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors.
Named for the 18th-century French explorer who documented it on one of his expeditions, this thorny ornamental vine produces colorful bracts around three small waxy flowers — which plant is it?
Historically hardware-dependent in size, ranging anywhere from 1 to 48 bits, this unit of digital information now almost always means eight bits — what's it called?
Byte: Unit of digital information, usually 8 bits.
With the formula H2CO3, this fleeting compound has a lifespan of only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature before converting to water and carbon dioxide — which compound?
Carbonic acid: Chemical compound. The molecule rapidly converts to water and carbon dioxide in the presence of water.
Nicknamed 'no-see-ums' for their tiny 1-3mm size, these biting midges are also among the best-studied pollinators of cocoa plants — what is this fly family called?
Ceratopogonidae: Family of flies commonly known as no see ums, or biting midges.
Usually triggered when a gallstone blocks the cystic duct, this inflammatory condition causes right-upper abdominal pain that radiates to the shoulder — what is it?
The smallest member of the cockatoo family and native to Australia, this crested pet bird is kept in an estimated 4.8 million US households — what bird is it?
Cockatiel: Species of bird. It is, therefore, now classified as the smallest subfamily of the Cacatuidae (cockatoo family).
Nicknamed the shaggy mane or lawyer's wig, this scaly white mushroom dissolves itself into black ink just hours after being picked — which fungus?
Coprinus comatus: Species of fungus. The young fruit bodies first appear as white cylinders emerging from the ground, then the bell-shaped caps open out.
This medical sign turns the lips, nail beds, and ear lobes a bluish-purple hue when blood isn't carrying enough oxygen, and comes in central and peripheral forms — what is it called?
Cyanosis: Decreased oxygen in the blood. Cyanosis is apparent usually in the body tissues covered with thin skin, including the mucous membranes, lips, nail beds, and ear lobes.
Often called eczema, this term covers skin inflammation marked by itchiness, redness and rash — sometimes with tiny blisters, sometimes thickening over time. What is it?
Dermatitis: Inflammatory disease of the skin.

Developed in the early 1950s to replace the propeller-driven Skyraider, this US Navy carrier jet had a maximum takeoff weight of just 24,500 pounds — about half the Navy's specification — which aircraft?
Douglas A-4 Skyhawk: Carrier-based attack aircraft.

This Russian political scientist studies authoritarian governance and legislative process, taught at Moscow institutions for nearly a decade, and by 2022 had a YouTube channel with a million subscribers — who is she?
Dubbed 'the father of nuclear physics,' this New Zealander won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry despite proposing that atoms have a tiny, densely charged nucleus — who is he?
Ernest Rutherford: New Zealand physicist and chemist (1871–1937)
Beloved in gardens for gobbling up pests, this spiny mammal native to Iberia and Scandinavia was introduced to New Zealand in the late 1800s but is now Red Listed in Britain — what is it?
European hedgehog: Species of small spiny mammal.
Historically used in the 18th century to track down escaped slaves, this large Brazilian dog breed of mastiff type now also serves as a guard dog and companion — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro: Brazilian breed of dog. The Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈfilɐ bɾaziˈlejɾu]) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.

Coated in cornmeal and pan-cooked while still unripe, this dish was originally a Northeastern and Midwestern staple before a hit movie rebranded it as quintessentially Southern comfort food — what is it?
Fried green tomatoes: American dish. Fried green tomatoes is a culinary dish usually found in the United States, made from unripe (green) tomatoes coated with cornmeal and fried.

A trained civil engineer who oversaw concerts at the Crystal Palace, this Englishman's program notes grew into a famous music dictionary — and he once hunted Vienna for lost Schubert manuscripts with Arthur Sullivan. Who was he?
George Grove: English engineer and writer on music (1820–1900)
This inflammatory arthritis brings on rapid, searing pain — often in the joint at the base of the big toe — caused by needle-shaped crystals of uric acid building up in the blood. What is it?
Gout: Form of arthritis causing swollen joints.
Its name literally combines words for 'holy' and 'flatfish,' reflecting its popularity on Catholic holy days — this demersal fish is prized both as food and as a sport catch. Which fish?
This field of study focuses on the methodological principles of interpreting texts — especially biblical and philosophical writings — and is closely related to exegesis. What is it called?
Hermeneutics: The study of the methodological principles of interpretation. As necessary, hermeneutics may include the art of understanding and communication.
In Greek myth, this fragrant spring bulb sprang from the blood of a youth slain by a jealous west wind god who coveted his bond with Apollo — what flower is it?
Co-creator of the AlexNet neural network and former chief scientist at OpenAI, this computer scientist has won NeurIPS's Test of Time Award three years running — who is he?

This Mexican neurophysiologist studied shamanism, meditation, and telepathy through the scientific method, wrote more than 50 books on the subjects, and then vanished without a trace in December 1994 — who was he?
Jacobo Grinberg: Mexican pseudoscientist, neurophysiologist and psychologist.
This English mathematician dreamed up the cellular automaton known as the Game of Life and spent his later years at Princeton — who was he?
Also called Bushman's tea, the leaves of this East African shrub are chewed as a recreational stimulant, most popular among Somalis and Yemenis — what is it?
Soft, dense, and bluish-silver when freshly cut, this heavy metal carries the highest atomic number of any stable element — and its Latin name, plumbum, gives it the symbol Pb. Which element is it?
Lead: Chemical element with atomic number 82 (Pb)
Understood before 1950 purely as the ability to decode written words, this concept later expanded to include the social and cultural dimensions of reading and writing — what skill is it?
Literacy: Ability to read and write.
Encoded by the codons AAA and AAG, this basic, essential amino acid cannot be synthesized by the human body — which one is it?
Lysine: Amino acid. Lysine (symbol Lys or K) is an α-amino acid that is a precursor to many proteins.

The first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the first person to win two, this Polish-born physicist and chemist discovered revolutionary elements and shared groundbreaking research on radioactivity with her husband—making her one of history's most influential scientists. Who was she?
Marie Curie: Polish-French physicist and chemist (1867–1934)
Nicknamed 'meow meow' and chemically related to compounds in the khat plant, this synthetic stimulant produces effects similar to MDMA and was first synthesized in 1929 — which drug?
Mephedrone: Recreational drug. Mephedrone, also known as 4-methylmethcathinone, 4-MMC, or 4-methylephedrone, is a synthetic stimulant drug belonging to the amphetamine and cathinone classes.
Known to NATO as 'Halo,' this Soviet-designed aircraft holds the record as the largest helicopter ever built in serial production — which one?
Mil Mi-26: Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter.

This Japanese biologist used diffusion equations to calculate how likely a gene is to take over a population, and in 1968 proposed the "neutral theory" that genetic drift, not just selection, drives molecular evolution — who was he?
First identified from an 1856 fossil in a German valley, this group of archaic humans roamed Europe and Asia until vanishing around 40,000 years ago as modern humans arrived — who were they?

Flown by William J. Knight to a record 4,520 mph in 1967 — a mark that still stands — this rocket-powered aircraft was part of an experimental series operated by the Air Force and NASA — which aircraft?
North American X-15: Rocket-powered aircraft and spaceplane operated by the US Air Force and NASA.
The most arboreal of the great apes, with long arms, short legs and reddish-brown hair, this genus Pongo primate survives today only in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra — what is it?
Orangutan: Genus of Asian apes. The most arboreal of the great apes, orangutans spend most of their time in trees.
Commonly known as the bullet ant for its notoriously painful sting, which insect species inhabits the humid lowland rainforests of Central and South America?
Often triggered by a ruptured appendix or a perforated gallbladder, this inflammation of the abdominal lining causes severe pain and swelling — what is it?

Peritonitis: Inflammation of abdominal organ lining. Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
Scientifically named Cajanus cajan, this perennial Fabaceae legume is a staple crop across the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean — what is it?
Pigeon pea: Species of perennial legume. The pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) is a perennial legume from the family Fabaceae native to the Eastern Hemisphere.
Though they look like dolphins, these small toothed whales are actually closer kin to narwhals and belugas, with flat spade-shaped teeth instead of dolphins' cone-shaped ones — what are they called?
Porpoise: Small cetacean of the family Phocoenidae.
This holotropical bird family comprises a dozen Afrotropical species and some 167 Neotropical species, including the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which family is this?
Psittacidae: Family of birds. The family Psittacidae or holotropical parrots is one of three families of true parrots.
After his Jewish family fled Germany, this engineer at Sanders Associates dreamed up playing games on a TV screen and built a 'Brown Box' that became the first home video game console — who is he?
Ralph H. Baer: American inventor and engineer (1922–2014)
This English anatomist coined the word 'Dinosauria' — 'terrible reptile' — yet remained an outspoken critic of Darwin's theory of natural selection — who is it?
Richard Owen: English biologist and palaeontologist (1804–1892)
Also known as brewer's or baker's yeast, this single-celled fungus believed to have originated on grape skins is one of biology's most-studied model organisms — which species?
Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Species of yeast. The species has been instrumental in winemaking, baking, and brewing since ancient times.
Covered in a spiny shell called a test and moving via tiny tube feet, this globular ocean-floor animal grazes mostly on algae — what creature is it?
Sea urchin: Class of marine invertebrates.
This small, wingless, primitive insect gets its common name from its grey sheen and darting, fish-like movements — and its scientific name hints at a diet of sugars and starches. What is it?
Silverfish: Small land insect in the order Zygentoma.
Also called dinkel wheat, this high-protein relict crop has been a staple in parts of Europe since the Bronze Age and is considered a hexaploid hybrid of common wheat and emmer — what is it?
Spelt: Species of wheat. It is a relict crop, eaten in Central Europe and northern Spain.

This speech disorder involves involuntary repetitions and prolongations of sounds or words, affects roughly 1% of the world's population, and is unrelated to a person's ability to structure their thoughts — what's it called?
Stuttering: Speech disorder. Persistent stuttering into adulthood often leads to outcomes detrimental to overall mental health, such as social isolation and suicidal thoughts.
This genus contains every living species of a large, snout-nosed herbivorous mammal, including the Malayan form sometimes split into its own genus — what is it?
Tapirus: Genus of tapir. The Malayan tapir is usually included in Tapirus as well, although some authorities have moved it into its own genus, Acrocodia.
Deaf from childhood and largely self-taught, this American began as a railroad telegrapher tinkering with telegraph systems before becoming a legendary inventor — who was he?
Thomas Edison: American inventor and businessman (1847–1931)
This medication — a synthetic version of the amino building block lysine — helps prevent excessive bleeding from trauma, surgery, or childbirth by blocking clot breakdown — what is it?

German and Russian teams keep trying and failing to synthesize this hypothetical element 120 — an alkaline earth metal of interest because it may sit in the "island of stability." What's its placeholder name?
Unbinilium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 120 (Ubn)
Native from Morocco and Portugal east to Iran, this flowering plant species includes thousands of varieties whose fruit is eaten fresh or dried into raisins and currants — what species is it?
Vitis vinifera: Species of flowering plant in the grape vine family.
The largest wild member of the dog family, it can still breed fertile hybrids with coyotes and jackals, and counts the domestic dog and dingo among its many subspecies — what animal is it?
The symbol for roentgenium is Rg. Roentgenium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
The symbol for gold is Au. Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au and atomic number 79.
